summary: The note describes Shiraz as the economic center of southern Iran and traces how its economy changed in the second half of the 19th century, after the Suez Canal opened in 1869 and European factory goods and new cash crops reached the region. It then outlines the city's present economic base: provincial agricultural products, a range of local industries, an oil refinery, and a large share of Iran's electronic industry.
one_line: Overview of Shiraz's economy, from 19th-century trade changes after the Suez Canal opened to its modern industries and electronics sector.
key_facts: Shiraz is the economic center of southern Iran.
The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 allowed extensive import into southern Iran of inexpensive European factory-made goods.
European factory-made goods reached southern Iran either directly from Europe or via India.
Farmers in unprecedented numbers began planting cash crops such as opium poppy, tobacco, and cotton.
Many export crops passed through Shiraz on their way to the Persian Gulf.
Iranian long-distance merchants from Fars developed marketing networks for these commodities.
Fars merchants established trading houses in Bombay, Calcutta, Port Said, Istanbul and even Hong Kong.
Shiraz's economic base is in its provincial products, which include grapes, citrus fruits, cotton and rice.
Industries in Shiraz such as cement production, sugar, fertilizers, textile products, wood products, metalwork and rugs dominate the local economy.
Shiraz has a major oil refinery.
Shiraz is a major center for Iran's electronic industries.
53% of Iran's electronic investment has been centered in Shiraz.
